conviction_note: Nothing on UAL is both company-specific and unpriced. Q3 is likely near the cut-down ~$2.60 bar, because UAL's July guide was set on the post-spike July 14 curve while Delta's was not. The Q4/FY guide will be cut on current fuel (UAL's own new policy), but the Street FY bar is disputed ($7.94 vs a stale $9.66), and the stock is already -14.8% over 20 days with upside skew paid. So abs_move 5.8 (implied 5.41 plus a likely guidance change) with p_up 49; findings sum -0.25, and the two numbers agree in being near zero.
bar: Q3 adjusted EPS ~$2.60 (Zacks $2.60, cut 18.5% in 60 days to $2.68 per Zacks; $2.59/$2.57 in other previews: https://finviz.com/news/403215/earnings-preview-united-airlines-stock-vulnerable-to-downgrades, https://investwithcolby.substack.com/p/ual-united-airlines-is-31-off-its), revenue ~$17.84-17.89B (+17%). Company Q3 guide $2.50-3.50 at $3.69/gal all-in fuel (July 14 curve), FY26 $9.00-11.00 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000100517/000010051726000135/ual_erx06302026xex992.htm). The Q4/FY Street bar is DISPUTED: FY $7.94 (implies Q4 ~$2.17, unattributed substack 2026-10-18) against FY $9.66 / Q3 $3.03 (Barchart via Yahoo, clearly stale: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/heres-expect-united-airlines-next-063112518.html), and Benzinga shows a stale Q4 $3.66. Guidance findings are capped small for that reason.

findings.finding: Q3 fuel ran above UAL's guide basis, but by less than it did for Delta. Gulf Coast jet spot averaged ~$3.84/gal in Q3 (FRED: Jul 3.403, Aug 3.724, Sep ~4.39 daily mean). UAL guided Q3 at $3.69 all-in on the July 14 curve (spot that day $3.552), and the curve had already absorbed the early-July jump ($575M = $1.12/share). Delta guided at $3.15 on ~July 9, realised $3.61 (+$0.46/gal, >$500M absorbed) and printed $1.72, $0.53 under its $2.25 guide midpoint, i.e. almost no incremental recapture. Applying Delta's behaviour to UAL's smaller gap (est. +$0.15-0.30/gal on ~1.27B gallons, ~$0.40-0.75/share) puts UAL near $2.30-2.70 against the $2.60 bar, which is inside the company's guided range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: UAL beat EPS in 11 of its last 12 quarters but rose after only 5 of them (Finviz/Zacks preview). July 2026: Q2 beat with a Q3 guide below the Street, -1.79%. April 2026: Q1 beat ($1.19 vs $1.08) with an FY cut, -5.58%. The reported quarter has not driven the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: Q3 consensus was cut 18.5% in 60 days to the bottom of the guide. If the market expected a clear miss, the bar would sit below $2.50 and the skew would be put-bid; it is call-bid. What may not be fully priced is that Delta showed near-zero incremental fuel recapture in Q3, while a ~$2.60 bar assumes UAL recaptures much of its post-guide fuel.
findings.independence: Delta Q3 2026 (guide $2.00-2.50 at $3.15/gal, actual $1.72, fuel $3.61): https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx and https://finviz.com/news/400853/delta-air-lines-shares-fall-as-third-quarter-earnings-miss-forecasts-and-full-year-outlook-is-cut. UAL guide basis from its 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000100517/000010051726000135/ual_erx06302026xex992.htm. This shares the fuel series with the Q4 guidance finding but a different quarter and line.

findings.finding: UAL's July update introduced 'a new policy to base its guidance on the most current fuel prices'. October Gulf Coast jet spot is $4.31-4.62/gal (Oct 1-14; $4.562 on Oct 14), about $0.6/gal above the Q3 average and ~$1/gal above the July 14 spot, with Brent back above $105 on Oct 8 and Hormuz still shut. The $9-11 FY guide needs Q4 of ~$3.2-5.2 after Q1 $1.19, Q2 $1.99 and Q3 ~$2.6, so a FY cut to roughly $7.5-8.5 is near-mechanical. The direction is known; the size against a disputed Street FY bar ($7.94 vs $9.66) is what is open.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: UAL's own: an April 2026 FY cut from $12-14 to $7-11 took -5.58%, and a July 2026 FY low-end raise with a soft Q3 guide took -1.79%. Delta on 2026-10-09: FY cut from $6.50-7.50 to $5.10-5.60 (24% at the midpoint, but only ~2% under its $5.46 consensus) and Q4 midpoint $1.40 vs $1.42 consensus; shares about -3% in the morning.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock is -14.8% in 20 days and -28% from its high, and Delta's cut already set the template. What may remain is that the guide is struck at the peak-October curve (above Delta's $4.25 Q4 all-in, since UAL has no refinery). If the market had fully priced a cut below $7.94 the skew would not be call-bid. The bar is disputed, so this is capped small.
findings.independence: Fuel levels: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DJFUELUSGULF (2026-10-15). Brent >$105 on 2026-10-08: https://www.quiverquant.com/news/United+Airlines+Falls+as+Higher+Oil+and+Pre-Earnings+Caution+Weigh+on+Shares. FY consensus $7.94: https://investwithcolby.substack.com/p/ual-united-airlines-is-31-off-its (unsourced).

findings.finding: Pricing power is still accelerating into Q4, which supports UAL's TRASM and the fuel recapture. September airfare CPI was +22.4% y/y and up 1.2% m/m, the third straight monthly rise. Delta (2026-10-09) printed Q3 revenue +16% on flat capacity (main cabin unit revenue +17%, domestic +16%), guided Q4 revenue ~+20% y/y, and said momentum continues across all products and geographies. UAL itself guided Q3 and Q4 TRASM above Q2's +12.1% with capacity capped at +2%, and its Q2 had premium +16% and corporate +27%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: strong revenue (+16%, TRASM +12.1%) did not stop -1.79% when fuel dominated the guide. Revenue strength has been necessary but not sufficient for this name in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: CPI and Delta's guide are public, and the Q3 revenue bar (+17%) already assumes TRASM in the mid-teens. Unpriced only to the extent that a Q4 revenue guide near +20% for UAL offsets part of the fuel cut. If priced, the Q4/FY bar would not have been cut as far as $7.94 FY.
findings.independence: Delta Q4 revenue guide ~+20% with continuing momentum: https://www.rttnews.com/3697924/delta-stock-drops-on-cautious-earnings-view-in-q4-fy26-after-weak-q3.aspx. Kirby on 2026-08-25: 'not even a blip in demand', 100% recovery expected in Q4: https://www.hotel-online.com/news/united-ceo-expects-gradual-fare-increases-in-2027-as-demand-stays-strong. UAL TRASM guide: the 8-K above.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is washed out rather than crowded. Spot $98.21 is -14.76% over 20 days and -27.85% from the 52-week high. 25d skew is -3.48 (calls bid) and put/call OI is 0.55. Short interest fell from 23.5M (07-31) to 16.8M (09-30), 4.2 days to cover. 23 of 25 brokers rate Buy, with a ~$151-155 mean target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: 4 up / 4 down over the last eight prints, median |move| 3.01%. The largest was +14.33% on 2025-07-09 (relief after a drawdown). UAL rose after only 5 of 11 recent beats, so washed-out entries have not reliably bounced.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price, so this is the market's own lean, not an edge. It is filed because it sets how far a guide cut that merely meets the cut-down bar can push the stock. If the market were braced for worse than consensus, puts would be bid.
findings.independence: Sealed baseline skew -3.48 and run-up (research file, 2026-10-20). Analyst counts: https://finviz.com/news/403215/earnings-preview-united-airlines-stock-vulnerable-to-downgrades.

findings.finding: TSA checkpoint volume was down y/y through the summer: August 2026 76.8M vs 80.3M (-4.4%), July -2.1%, and early September flat (16.44M vs 16.41M). Industry passenger volume is shrinking while fares carry revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No UAL reaction tied to TSA data. The Q2 2026 load-factor and yield mix was absorbed in a -1.79% fuel-driven move.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and largely explained by industry capacity cuts. A broader series (airfare CPI +22%, Delta revenue +16%) says revenue is fine, so this narrow proxy is sized below it. It matters only if UAL's load factor slips.
findings.independence: Proxy only. It runs against the revenue finding (https://airwaysmag.com/new-post/us-airline-fares-september-2026-inflation), which is the broader series.

findings.finding: The flight attendant contract (ratified May 2026) carries an average 31% raise this summer plus boarding pay (~7-8% more compensation) and $741M in retro pay. It lifts Q3/Q4 CASM-ex (Q2 CASM-ex was already +6.1%), but it was known before, and inside, the July guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced: it lands inside guidance given two months after ratification. It matters only if 2027 CASM commentary surprises.

baseline_tension: The fuel negatives agree with the 20-day run-up (-14.8%) and cut against the skew (-3.48, upside paid). The option market leans toward relief after a guide cut it largely expects, and I have no document showing the cut will be worse than a disputed bar, so p_up sits near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (disputed bar): the Q4/FY Street bar has two disagreeing sources ($7.94 vs $9.66), so the fuel-guidance finding was capped from -0.8 to -0.6 and p_up moved from 48 to 49.
Rules 1 and 6 (inside the guide, name sells beats): the Q3 fuel finding lands inside the $2.50-3.50 range, so it went from -0.5 to -0.3.

Rule 5 (proxy vs broader series): airfare CPI is an industry proxy, though Delta is a direct peer that printed after UAL last spoke, so it went from +0.6 to +0.4. TSA volume runs against the broader revenue series, so it went from -0.2 to -0.1.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): the flight attendant contract was known before the July guide, so it went from -0.1 to -0.05.
Rule 7: short interest was looked up before the negatives (16.8M, 4.2 days, falling); not crowded, so no squeeze haircut. The positioning finding agrees with the skew and was left at +0.5.
